key_insight: Multiwavelength photoluminescence non-destructively reveals depth-dependent UV damage in perovskite solar cells, with degradation concentrated near the buried hole-transport-layer interface.
engineering_relevance: Depth-sensitive optical screening can guide interface design, including 3-mercaptopropyltrimethoxysilane modification to improve UV stability.
method: Use wavelength-dependent absorption to probe different depths.
Combine wide-field PL imaging, time-resolved PL, and ideality-factor measurements during UV soaking.
Compare perovskite films and p-i-n devices with different ITO interface modifiers.
evidence_signal: Nondestructive measurements localized preferential UV degradation to the HTL interface, consistent with ex-situ destructive tests, and showed reduced damage with silane modification.
watch_item: The abstract reports no quantitative stability gains or validation under broader operational stress conditions.
paper_title: Multiwavelength Photoluminescence as a Non-destructive Probe of Depth-Dependent UV Damage in Perovskite Semiconductors
